text: Inverse power flow is an important and interesting problem in power system engineering. This paper investigates the problem of inverse power flow. The problem of inverse power flow is an unusual and interesting problem in power system engineering as it is different from the problem of power flow in the power system. In the problem of power flow in the power system, power surges travels in reverse direction as compared to the problem of inverse power flow. The problem of inverse power flow is an important and interesting problem in power system engineering as power systems are used for distributed generations such as the solar panels. The full mathematical formulation of the problem of inverse power flow is discussed in this paper. The constraints should be taken into account in the problem of inverse power flow with respect to voltage and power limits. The solution of the problem of inverse power flow with the help of optimization algorithms is discussed in this paper. Case studies are also presented in this paper in order to depict the applications of the problem of inverse power flow in the power system engineering. The problem of inverse power flow is an important and interesting problem in power system engineering as it is the basis of the exact and efficient control of power flows in complex power systems. The problem of inverse power flow in the development of smart grid is also discussed in this paper.

First we are going to analyze the frequency of abstracts in the manuscripts that are published in the journal Nature Genetics. Is there any difference in the frequency of abstracts between authors, issues or fields of specialization? We are going to detect the significant association, but there is no difference in frequency of abstracts with respect to the Journal number (JSS). Then we are going to analyze the selective publication in the journal Nature Genetics with respect to the geographical location and also the corresponding geographical Journal issues with respect to whether they are journals (SSJ) or journals at the top of field of specialization. We are going to detect the same result. New analysis and new hypotheses are proposed. First analysis of the selective publication : In this analysis we are going to compute the frequency of abstracts with respect to the author, issue and the field of specialization. In this analysis, we are going to use the logistic regression model to estimate the frequency of abstracts with respect to the author, the issue and the field of specialization. From the estimate we are going to propose two hypotheses. (i) Journals publish the manuscripts with same quality within the same field of specialization. (ii) Journals publish only those manuscripts which are not having any papers or manuscripts with small number of original articles. Second analysis of the selective publication : We are going to examine the manuscripts with respect to the author, issue and geographical location. We are going to detect that the frequency pattern of the abstracts and manuscripts are different for those manuscripts published in the top journals. The difference is going to be detected by taking into account the publication status and authorship by geographical location using a logistic regression analysis. text: We propose and analyze two new strategies to solve the segmentation problem of multiple organs in the deep learning context. The strategies are based on the use of the parallel input channels from the different planes with different supervisory strategy which can be used for solving the problem of ambiguity due to the presence of partial and irrelevant annotations in the semi-supervised strategies. We show how to extend the co-training supervisory strategy to different planes using a two-step strategy consisting of convolutional autoencoder and a 3D residual neural network. The proposed strategies are able to capture the complementarity of appearance and geometry representation from input images and are able to achieve significant improvement over the performance of unimodal input single planes and end-to-end deep learning strategies. We show that similar performance can be achieved by employing similar strategies on similar algorithms. The performance achieved on 5 public datasets containing brain tumour slices is the state of the art performance as compared to human experts without any interactive finetuning.
OG_text: Abstract: In this work, two novel methods are introduced to tackle the multi-organ segmentation using deep learning. Both proposed techniques exploit the idea of leveraging multiple input planes as parallel channels on which different supervision schemes can be defined so that information flow among such representations can better handle ambiguous signals coming from partial or irrelevant annotations (semi supervision) and also boost generalization to test images with occluded or rotated organs relative to training data. Specifically, instead of operating only in the spatial domain, co-training in our case is effectively achieved along both planes thanks to the combination between a convolutional autoencoder applied to extracting features from RGB channels (which mainly capture shape variations)and the application of 3D ResNets acting on a T2w/FLAIR subtraction volume used to convey anatomical details. Such components allow us to efficiently represent both appearance and geometry through complementary domains providing important contributions in terms of performance over standard approaches based on unimodal channels and end-to-end architectures. Our results show marked improvements w.r.t seminal MICCAI publications obtained applying similar algorithms. A quantitative comparison carried out on five public datasets including brain tumor slices demonstrates that by simply modifying the backbone architecture we exceed state-of-the-art scores achieving results comparable with human experts without the need for any form of interactive fine tuning.
NS10_text: Title Semi Supervised Multi Organ Segmentation via Deep Multi Planar Co-Training  Abstract, This paper presents a novel approach for multi organ segmentation leveraging the synergy of convolutional autoencoders and 3D ResNets to tackle the challenging and debilitating task of accurately segmenting multiple organs in medical images. The proposed method, denoted as Semi Supervised Multi Organ Segmentation via Deep Multi Planar Co Training (MS DMIC), draws inspiration from the pioneering work by Richard Szeliski "Computer Vision Algorithms and Applications" showcasing its potential to improve the reliability of such algorithms in challenging environments reminiscent of the work carried out by researchers at ETH Zurich and New York University (NYU).  Most existing segmentation algorithms rely on a single modality to segment organs such as the T1/T1-cen and T2-weighted images. In contrast, the proposed MS DMIC method exploits the synergy of multiple input planes, incorporating convolutional autoencoders to extract shape features from RGB channels (capturing variations mainly pertain to apparent organs displacements) and 3D ResNets to convey anatomical details using a subtraction T2w/FLAIR volume. This multi planar co-training approach enables MS DMIC to handle ambiguities in annotations (partial or irrelevant) while leveraging the strengths of two modalities. As evidenced by the seminal publication of Omar Lozano, "Automatic Segmentation of Brain Tumors Using CT MRI Images," this methodology outperforms existing state-of-the art approaches and reaches human the panel of experts in the field level segmentation accuracy.  The proposed MS DMIC method was evaluated on the open source 3D Brain tumor segmentation dataset and outperforms the MACS (Medical Image Computing and Computer Assisted Intervention grouping–validation) BCIS (Brain Tumor Image Segmentation) and MaLiMo dataset. Furthermore, the fact that simple architectural modifications to the convolutional spine led to a performance comparable to human experts indicates the potential to address common issues in deep learning-based segmentation, such as memorization in the training process.

Coconut Fudge Brownies
Ingredients
1 cup granulated sugar
1/2 cup unsalted butter (at room temperature)
1/4 cup melted coconut oil
2 large eggs
1 tsp vanilla extract
1 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
3/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
2 tsp baking powder
1/2 tsp salt
1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips
1/2 cup shredded coconut
Instructions
Preheat your oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). If you're using a fan furnace, use 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) instead. Grease the base of an 8 x 8-inch (20 x 20 cm) square tin with paper. Add granulated sugar, unsalted butter, and melted coconut oil to a large bowl. Whisk everything together until it's fluffy and light. Add the eggs one at a time. Make sure to whisk everything well after adding each egg. Add in the vanilla extract. Add all-purpose flour, unsweetened cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt to a medium bowl. Combine all the ingredients. Add everything together in the large bowl with the wet ingredients. Whisk everything until it's all combined. Add in semi-sweet chocolate chips and shredded coconut and mix everything together. Pour the batter into the lined tin. Use a spatula or the back of a spoon to level the batter in the pan. Put it into the oven and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until it comes out clean when you stick in a toothpick in the middle of it. Let everything cool down before you cut into squares. Once it's fully cool, you can cut it into squares and enjoy.

By employing a combination of experimental and theoretical techniques, we study the electronic structure and topological properties of Bi2Se3 as the thickness of the material is reduced from 3D to 2D. Our results show that the 3D Dirac cone of Bi2Se3 collapses into a pair of 2D Dirac cones at the edges of the Brillouin zone, resulting in the emergence of novel topological phases. Ingredients:  
1 bunch asparagus (about 1 pound)  
6 large eggs  
4 tablespoons unsalted butter  
4 thin slices prosciutto di Parma, chopped  
1/2 cup grated Pecorino Pepato cheese  
1/2 cup heavy cream  
1/2 teaspoon white pepper  
1/4 teaspoon salt  

Instructions:  
1. Boil water in a pot over high heat. While doing so, fill a large bowl with ice water and set aside. Trim the tips off the asparagus and set aside. Cut stalks into 1-inch pieces and set aside. Blanch the tips in boiling water for 1 minute. Transfer to ice water using a slotted spoon and chill for 1 minute. Drain, pat dry, and set aside. Blanch stalks for 4 to 6 minutes until tender. Drain, pat dry, and set aside.  
2. Crack eggs into individual ramekins or cups. Heat a large skillet with water and add vinegar. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Carefully lower eggs into water and cook 3 to 5 minutes until whites set and yolks are cooked to preference. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on towel.  
3. Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add prosciutto and cook 2 to 3 minutes until crisp. Add asparagus and cook 2 to 3 minutes until tender-crisp. Stir in cheese and cook 1 minute until melted. Add cream, pepper, and salt; heat through.  
4. Serve by dividing asparagus and prosciutto onto individual plates. Place a poached egg atop each and add cheese sauce.

It is here a problem of interest to the research groups at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) who have developed modern algorithms for signal processing in radar systems. Lavish Lemon Cake Recipe  

Ingredients:  
- 2 cups all-purpose flour  
- 1½ teaspoons baking powder  
- ¼ teaspoon salt  
- 3 large eggs, room temperature  
- 1 cup granulated sugar  
- 2 tablespoons lemon zest  
- ¾ cup fresh lemon juice  
- 1 cup buttermilk, room temperature  
- ½ cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled  
- 2 teaspoons vanilla extract  

Instructions:  

1. Preheat oven to 350°F (176°C) and grease a 9x13 inch baking pan with cooking spray or butter, then flour it.  

2. In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.  

3. In a large bowl, beat eggs and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes with an electric mixer. Fold in lemon zest and juice until blended.  

4. Gradually add dry ingredients to wet mix, alternating with buttermilk, starting and ending with dry components. Mix until just combined.  

5. Stir in cooled melted butter and vanilla extract until thoroughly mixed.  

6. Pour batter into prepared pan and smooth surface with spatula. Bake 25–30 minutes or until toothpick inserted comes out clean.  

7. Let cake cool completely before glazing. Combine powdered sugar and lemon juice in a small bowl until smooth. Drizzle over cake and let set before serving. Enjoy!

Coconut Fudge Brownies Recipe  

Ingredients:  
- 1 cup granulated sugar  
- ½ cup unsalted butter, softened  
- ¼ cup coconut oil, melted  
- 2 large eggs  
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract  
- 1 ½ cups all-purpose flour  
- ¾ cup unsweetened cocoa powder  
- 2 teaspoons baking powder  
- ½ teaspoon salt  
- 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips  
- ½ cup shredded coconut  

Instructions:  
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and line an 8x8 inch pan with parchment paper.  
2. In a large bowl, beat sugar, butter, and coconut oil until creamy. Add eggs one at a time, beating thoroughly afterward. Stir in vanilla.  
3. In a medium bowl, mix flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt. Gradually incorporate into wet ingredients, stirring until combined.  
4. Fold in chocolate chips and shredded coconut until evenly distributed.  
5. Pour batter into prepared pan and smooth surface with spatula or spoon. Bake 25–30 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean.  
6. Cool completely before cutting and serving. Enjoy!

OG_text: In this paper, we present a novel uncertainty-aware self-ensembling (UA-SE) model for semi-supervised learning of 3D left atrium segmentation. The UA-SE model exploits the correlations between neighboring voxels and uses a self-ensemble strategy to enhance the representation power of semi-supervised learning. We employ a 3D residual UNet with an uncertainty estimation module to model the spatial correlations and output the uncertainty map. Furthermore, we propose a self-ensembling module that can model both the label and uncertainty simultaneously by considering the local graph structure. The proposed model is trained in a semi-supervised manner, where only a small portion of the labeled data is used for training, and the remaining unlabeled data are utilized to enhance the model's representation power. We evaluate the proposed method on the publicly available MICCAI 3D Slicer Tracking Challenge 2017 dataset. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed UA-SE model compared to the state-of-the-art semi-supervised learning methods. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/VITA-Group/UA-SE.

However, traditional semi-supervised learning methods often rely on limited labeled data, leading to suboptimal performance and uncertainty in segmentations. To address these challenges. We present the Uncertainty aware Self ensembling Model (UA-SE). Which leverages the correlations between neighboring voxels and self ensembling strategy to enhance the representation power of semi-supervised learning for 3D left atrium segmentation.  At the Medical Image Analysis Group (MIAG) of the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), researchers A. Tarfawi, B. GFX, and M. JITらい employed a 3D residual UNet with an uncertainty estimation module to model the spatial correlations and output the uncertainty map. The uncertainty estimation module, developed in collaboration with Dr. P. Triebitz of the Computing Infrastructure Facility of the Helmholtz Center for Health Research (SIGT), exploits the correlations between neighboring voxels to establish a reliable uncertainty map. Furthermore, the researchers proposed a self ensembling module that can model both the label and uncertainty simultaneously by considering the local graph structure, inspired by the work of the Computer Vision Group at the Technical University of Munich (TUM), led by Professor LS Haralick.  The proposed UA-SE model is trained in a semi-supervised manner, where only 20% of the labeled data is used for training. And the remaining unlabeled data are utilized to enhance the model's representation power. The performance of the UA-SE model is evaluated on the publicly available MICCAI 3D Slicer Tracking Challenge 2017 dataset. Which contains 15 subjects with segmentations of their 3D left atrium structures. The US government is seeking a new ruling against tobacco companies that could cost them up to $280bn (£155bn). The Department of Justice (DoJ) has asked a federal judge to impose a penalty on the industry for a "decades-long conspiracy to deceive the American public".

The move comes after a 2020 ruling in which the tobacco industry was found guilty of violating federal racketeering laws. The DoJ now wants the companies to surrender profits made through their alleged misconduct, which it claims spanned more than 50 years.

The case, which is one of the largest civil cases in US history, targets major tobacco companies including Philip Morris USA, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco, Brown & Williamson and Lorillard Tobacco. The government alleges that these companies deliberately misled the public about the health risks associated with smoking and the addictive nature of nicotine.

The $280bn figure is based on the government's estimate of profits from cigarette sales to underage smokers and smokers who were allegedly deceived by the companies' marketing tactics. The DoJ argues that these profits were ill-gotten and should be forfeited.

The tobacco industry has strongly denied the allegations and is expected to fight the penalty. They argue that the government's case is based on a flawed interpretation of the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act (RICO), the law under which the case is being pursued.

The industry also contends that the penalty is excessive and would lead to bankruptcy for many companies, resulting in job losses and harm to the economy. They further argue that they have already paid billions in settlements to individual states and have significantly changed their marketing practices in response to previous litigation.

The case is expected to be heard in the coming months. If the judge rules in favor of the DoJ, it could set a precedent for future cases against industries accused of deceptive practices. However, any ruling is likely to be appealed, potentially leading to years of further litigation.
